title: Indian-Origin Cricketers Wadia, Sharma Named in Cricket Australia Squads
excerpt: Mumbai-born Jerrssis Wadia earns selection in the CA XI to face Bangladesh in Darwin, while Victorian all-rounder Aryan Sharma joins the Men's Development Squad for the MRF Academy Program in Chennai.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • Jerrssis Wadia selected for CA XI to face Bangladesh in Darwin from August 6-8.
  • Aryan Sharma joins Australia's Men's Development Squad for MRF Academy Program in Chennai.
  • Wadia signed a two-year deal with Adelaide Strikers after impressive BBL|15 performance.
  • Sharma represented Australia at the 2026 ICC U19 World Cup and holds a rookie contract with Victoria.
  • Both players highlight the growing presence of Indian-origin cricketers in Australian cricket.

Two Pathways, Two Indian-Origin Cricketers

Cricket Australia has named India-born allrounder Jerrssis Wadia and Victorian allrounder Aryan Sharma in separate national pathway squads, marking a milestone for both players and the broader Indian diaspora cricket community in Australia.

Wadia, 24, has been selected in the CA XI squad that will face the Bangladesh men's Test team in a three-day warm-up match in Darwin from August 6 to 8. The South Australian left-hander and left-arm orthodox spinner progressed through Adelaide's Premier Cricket system with Tea Tree Gully before breaking into the Adelaide Strikers squad during the recent KFC BBL season.

Sharma, meanwhile, has been named in Australia's Men's Development Squad for the MRF Academy Program in Chennai. The squad will play two two-day matches during the program — scheduled for August 5–6 and August 10–11 — on traditionally spin-friendly wickets in India.

Wadia's Rapid Rise Through Australian Cricket

Born in Mumbai, Wadia played age-group cricket for the Baroda Cricket Association before moving to Adelaide at 17 to pursue professional cricket. His family has deep cricket roots: his grandfather Neville Wadia earned a place in the Guinness Book of World Records as the oldest player to score a century in minor cricket.

Wadia announced himself in the Big Bash League during BBL|15, smashing 34 off just 16 balls against the Brisbane Heat — a cameo that included three consecutive sixes and a four off successive deliveries. Across seven BBL matches for the Strikers, he scored 52 runs at a strike rate of 136.84 and claimed two wickets with his orthodox spin.

"I couldn't be more grateful to the Adelaide Strikers and the South Australian Cricket Association for the opportunity to play professional cricket. I loved my time wearing the Strikers blue and playing in front of the best fans in the world."

— Jerrssis Wadia, after signing a two-year deal with the Adelaide Strikers

His performances earned him a two-year contract extension with the Strikers and a full state contract with South Australia for the 2026-27 domestic season. He is one of several new additions to the Redbacks squad, alongside keeper Matt Gilkes from NSW and allrounder Noah McFadyen.

Sharma's U19 Pedigree

Aryan Sharma's selection in the Development Squad continues his progression through Cricket Australia's talent pathway. The Victorian allrounder represented Australia at the 2026 ICC Under-19 Men's Cricket World Cup in Zimbabwe and was also part of the Melbourne Stars squad during the most recent BBL season.

Sharma was earlier named in Australia's U19 squad for the home series against India in 2025, alongside fellow Indian-origin cricketer Yash Deshmukh. He has since earned a rookie contract with Cricket Victoria for the 2026-27 season, playing his Premier Cricket with Carlton.

The Development Squad in Chennai will be coached by former Australian wicketkeeper Tim Paine and Anthony Clark, while former Australian head coach Tim Nielsen will lead the CA XI in Darwin.

A Growing Diaspora Presence in Australian Cricket

Wadia and Sharma are part of a growing cohort of Indian-origin cricketers making inroads into the Australian domestic system. The 2026-27 state contract lists include several players of South Asian heritage across multiple states: Nikhil Chaudhary with Tasmania, Ashley Chandrasinghe with Victoria, Nivethan Radhakrishnan with Tasmania, Harjas Singh on an NSW rookie deal, and Nitesh Samuel on a Tasmania rookie contract.

Harjas Singh, who top-scored for Australia in their 2024 U19 World Cup final triumph over India, clubbed a record-breaking triple-century in Sydney first-grade cricket last October before earning his maiden state contract.

The representation reflects both Australia's multicultural demographics and Cricket Australia's expanding pathway programs, which are designed to identify talent across community and Premier Cricket leagues nationwide.

What's Next

Wadia will join a CA XI featuring the likes of Sam Konstas, Josh Philippe, and Teague Wyllie for the Bangladesh warm-up match in Darwin, an assignment that offers red-ball exposure against a touring international side. Sharma and the Development Squad head to Chennai for the MRF Academy Program, where conditions will test their adaptability on Indian surfaces — a valuable experience ahead of the Australian domestic summer.

Both squads assemble in early August, with the 2026-27 Sheffield Shield and BBL seasons beginning later in the year.
